title: Viral semantic rubric human-annotated benchmark
description: Human-annotated labels for the three 0-5 viral semantic dimensions. Each sample records the evidence features a human reader identified in the source text plus the level they assigned. Used to regression-test the deterministic rubric evaluator. NOT a replay of live LLM output.

coverage.boundary_cases: 7 explicitly annotated off-ladder cases plus 7 hook/tension/reuse grid anchors

annotation_protocol: Single annotator. Each sample was read by a human who first marked which evidence signals were literally present, then assigned a level using docs/design/03_Viral_Semantic_Analysis.md. There is no second annotator, so inter-annotator agreement is not measured.
known_limitations: Evidence features were annotated by hand, so the evaluator is measured against the same feature vocabulary it consumes.
No live-LLM replay: this does not prove the production model reaches these numbers.

The grid samples are constructed so the evidence ladder is internally consistent with the labelled level, which inflates accuracy; the 7 boundary samples are the only cases where the human label deliberately differs from the mechanical ladder, and they are what the MAE / exact-match gap reflects.
MVP scale only; not statistically representative.

A stake is named but nothing is at risk yet, so a human reads it as weak friction. A problem is stated without any complication being flagged.
Escalation is present but maximum pressure only lands later in the piece, so this beat is annotated as peak rather than as escalation.
A reusable shape is visible even though no vague-shape flag was set, so reuse is annotated one level up. The problem is implied by the minor complication.
Two mechanics transfer cleanly but the article-specific devices are not reusable, so a human reads 'most transfers' rather than 'mechanism transfers'.
The skeleton is reusable but every device that made it work is article-specific, so reuse is downgraded to shape-only.
